instrucciones:
Recibes registros de una base de reglas de producción audiovisual con IA (texto completo, puede estar en
inglés, ruso o español). Para CADA registro devuelve:
- "enunciado": la regla en español, UNA frase, sin adornos: qué exige, prohíbe, limita o especifica. Si el registro
  es un ejemplo o una explicación sin norma, di qué ilustra ("Ejemplo: ...", "Explicación: ...").
- "alcance": a qué aplica exactamente (modelo y versión, caso T1-T5, etapa, tipo de pieza, régimen) o "general".
- "temas": de 1 a 3 claves de la lista, las que mejor describen de qué trata la regla.

[Race, speed and faceless kinetic montage › 2. Four schools worth stealing] **Race-truth (Frankenheimer, Lelouch, Mangold/Papamichael, Howard/Dod Mantle, Refn).** Speed is a fact you earn by putting the camera where a real rig could bolt — bumper, hood lip, hostess-tray, axle, cabin. Low, wide and close, hard-mounted without vibration isolation so "cheeks shake", asphalt streaking in frame as the speedometer, mini-cams next to pistons and swelling tires for "an electron-microscope view of the car at its limit". Refn's cocoon: silence and stillness inside the shell, chaos outside, so the launch detonates. Refuse the crank — *Grand Prix* oiled tires for real smoke rather than fake the burnout.
→ **Rule:** if the implied camera could not physically mount on the car, the panel reads as render — drop it to bumper height and bolt it on.

[Race, speed and faceless kinetic montage › 2. Four schools worth stealing] **Loaded composition (Bong, Park, Anderson, Kon).** With no faces, geometry and the depth stack do the acting (the FG/MG/BG depth method is `animatic-keyframes.md` §6). One geometric spine (centerline or Christmas Tree as the axis); every object an evidence (Park: "each object is a clue") or it is cut. Symmetry is handwriting — one held symmetric "breath" frame says balanced rivalry; break it the instant one car noses ahead. Kon's graphic-match pairs compress time across two adjacent keyframes sharing a shape at the same size and screen position.
→ **Rule:** a panel answers one question in the first glance and rewards a second look — one focal point, one emotion, three depth layers, zero dead objects.

[Race, speed and faceless kinetic montage › 2. Four schools worth stealing] **Rule-based ad (Honda *Cog*, Audi Quattro, Nike/Ritchie, Goodyear).** The drama is pure mechanism: every object does something irreversible, "let the machine talk" (no music), the entire spot first-person with no hero face. Tension is "will it fire". A static fetish shot of a gear lever flatlines; an object crossing a threshold says a decision just happened.
→ **Rule:** objects carry feeling only when they visibly **change state** — board the "after" (needle pinned in the red, ignition lamp blooming live, slick caught mid-fold), the "before" is implied.

[Race, speed and faceless kinetic montage › 3. Selling speed in a single frame] A still has no engine note and zero motion. It sells velocity through the **speed-budget rule** — a frame reads fast only when **≥3 of five cues coexist** (camera at/below bumper height · asphalt streaking the lower frame · a near foreground reference passing the edge · sharp hero against motion-blurred background · a mechanical-vibration cue). The full rule, with the anti-fake firewall, lives in `animatic-keyframes.md` §4; do not re-derive it. One cue is a car photo; three is velocity; five and even a parked car reads dangerous. If a "fast" panel can't name three, reframe lower, drag the camera to the asphalt, throw a barrier into the foreground.

[Race, speed and faceless kinetic montage › 3. Selling speed in a single frame] Two race-domain extensions the general file does not carry:
**The foreground reference catalog** (cue *c*, the cheapest and strongest speed multiplier). Place the reference *near the lens* (so it smears most) and *passing the edge* (so it reads as transiting, not parked). Keep one near object tack-sharp so the brain measures the smear against it.

[Race, speed and faceless kinetic montage › 3. Selling speed in a single frame] Reference object: Cone / timing block · Where to place it: near edge, elongated/smeared · Speed it implies: lane-level rush

[Race, speed and faceless kinetic montage › 3. Selling speed in a single frame] Reference object: Armco barrier / wall · Where to place it: scraping the near side, streaked · Speed it implies: proximity + velocity

[Race, speed and faceless kinetic montage › 3. Selling speed in a single frame] Reference object: Lane stripe / chevron · Where to place it: lower frame, smeared toward bottom · Speed it implies: ground speed

[Race, speed and faceless kinetic montage › 3. Selling speed in a single frame] Reference object: Christmas-Tree pylon · Where to place it: foreground, sharp anchor; car blurred · Speed it implies: launch reference + timer

[Race, speed and faceless kinetic montage › 3. Selling speed in a single frame] Reference object: Tree / lamp post / grandstand · Where to place it: whipping past, motion-rod · Speed it implies: open-road pace

[Race, speed and faceless kinetic montage › 3. Selling speed in a single frame] Reference object: Tire smoke / spray · Where to place it: raked by backlight across frame · Speed it implies: force + air movement

[Race, speed and faceless kinetic montage › 3. Selling speed in a single frame] Reference object: Marshal / crowd at periphery · Where to place it: blurred, fragmented · Speed it implies: scale + danger

[Race, speed and faceless kinetic montage › 3. Selling speed in a single frame] **Long-lens compression** — the second speed register and the antidote to "only blur sells speed". Frankenheimer's 1000mm stacked distant cars onto the hero so closing distance reads as collapse. Pair compression panels with low-wide panels in the cut; never board the whole spot on one lens. In `seedance.md`/`veo.md` syntax name "motion blur, fast-shutter look on background, sharp subject" explicitly — models default to over-clean stabilization (the prompt skeleton is `animatic-keyframes.md` §7).
[Race, speed and faceless kinetic montage › 3. Selling speed in a single frame] (The full "what kills the speed" audit lives once, in §10.)

[Race, speed and faceless kinetic montage › 4. Storytelling without faces — the race captioning system] A face does four jobs: internal state, where it looks, the cost, the decision. Banned, those jobs redistribute — **decision → anatomy mid-action; internal state → an object crossing a threshold; looking/rivalry → space.** The mechanism, the EMOTION→OBJECT substitution table and the state-change cheat-sheet are owned by `animatic-keyframes.md` §5; do not duplicate them. Two filters before you draw: name the **verb** on any hand/foot panel (grip / latch / shift / preload / release — no verb, no panel), and board only the **after** state of any object threshold (Honda *Cog*). Pick ONE hero object and board it three times at rising intensity — beats twelve unrelated inserts (`dramaturgy.md` §13).

[Race, speed and faceless kinetic montage › 4. Storytelling without faces — the race captioning system] What this file owns is the **race captioning system** — the margin label that proves an insert is load-bearing (Law 6). Every detail keyframe gets exactly one. If you cannot assign one, drop the panel.

[Race, speed and faceless kinetic montage › 4. Storytelling without faces — the race captioning system] Label: **setup** · Story job: establishes capability / readiness · Typical object / crop: glove pull, harness latch, ignition dead · Skill tag (`role-modes.md` §4): Establish / Detail

[Race, speed and faceless kinetic montage › 4. Storytelling without faces — the race captioning system] Label: **commitment** · Story job: point of no return chosen · Typical object / crop: foot pins throttle, shifter rammed home, ignition live · Skill tag (`role-modes.md` §4): Shift / Impact

[Race, speed and faceless kinetic montage › 4. Storytelling without faces — the race captioning system] Label: **mistake** · Story job: something slips / over-limit · Typical object / crop: tire shake, wheel fights back, revs flare wrong · Skill tag (`role-modes.md` §4): Pressure / Impact

[Race, speed and faceless kinetic montage › 4. Storytelling without faces — the race captioning system] Label: **recovery** · Story job: control reclaimed · Typical object / crop: hand catches the correction, tach settles back into band · Skill tag (`role-modes.md` §4): Shift

[Race, speed and faceless kinetic montage › 4. Storytelling without faces — the race captioning system] Label: **proof-of-speed** · Story job: force is real, not staged · Typical object / crop: chassis squat, slick wrinkle, exhaust flame, asphalt streak · Skill tag (`role-modes.md` §4): Power / Pressure

[Race, speed and faceless kinetic montage › 4. Storytelling without faces — the race captioning system] Label: **result** · Story job: who won the inch · Typical object / crop: finish stripe, slicks ballooned at trap, one nose ahead, chute bloom · Skill tag (`role-modes.md` §4): Impact / Aftermath
[Race, speed and faceless kinetic montage › 4. Storytelling without faces — the race captioning system] (Banned panels are consolidated in §10.)

[Race, speed and faceless kinetic montage › 5. The race ritual (liturgy) + the 5 shot families] The race is not a chase, it is a *liturgy*. Every phase is a legible, irreversible state-change a knowing viewer reads instantly — muddle the order and the spot dies. The countdown *tightens cut length toward the green*, then explodes: the drag-specific instance of the `dramaturgy.md` §12 rhythm staircase. Draw one anchor keyframe per beat. In a faceless spot **Reaction** is reassigned from a human face to the *machine's* face — the needle jumping, the slick wrinkling, the nose squatting. Gauges and rubber are the actor.

The race ritual (liturgy) + the 5 shot families] #: 1 · Ritual beat: Water box entry · Function: Establish · Keyframe to draw (still): Front slick easing into mirror-still water, chalk/box edge in frame, bulbs reflected in the sheet · Light (cold): Steel-blue dusk, wet specular · Emotion: coiled stillness

[Race, speed and faceless kinetic montage › 5. The race ritual (liturgy) + the 5 shot families] #: 2 · Ritual beat: Burnout (white→blue) · Function: Power · Keyframe to draw (still): Ground-level wall of smoke off the rear, plume backlit; car straining on line-lock · Light (cold): Hard cyan backlight through smoke · Emotion: barely-leashed force

[Race, speed and faceless kinetic montage › 5. The race ritual (liturgy) + the 5 shot families] #: 3 · Ritual beat: Reverse settle · Function: Pressure · Keyframe to draw (still): Rear rolling back through its own drifting smoke toward the beams, tail-lights bleeding red into haze · Light (cold): Smoke haze, low key, red tail wash · Emotion: deliberate menace

The race ritual (liturgy) + the 5 shot families] #: 4 · Ritual beat: Pre-stage bulb · Function: Pressure · Keyframe to draw (still): Front tyre creeping, top blue bulb lit as anchor, beam line as a graphic spine on asphalt · Light (cold): Blue bulb glow on wet metal · Emotion: held breath

The race ritual (liturgy) + the 5 shot families] #: 10 · Ritual beat: The pass · Function: Power · Keyframe to draw (still): Joust / parallel tracking, asphalt streaking, rival lane in frame · Light (cold): Streaked specular, motion-rod lights · Emotion: duel

[Race, speed and faceless kinetic montage › 5. The race ritual (liturgy) + the 5 shot families] #: 11 · Ritual beat: Finish · Function: Impact · Keyframe to draw (still): Top-end: slicks "blown up"/distorted, cars inches apart crossing the line, one nose ahead · Light (cold): Cold-white finish pool · Emotion: margin

[Race, speed and faceless kinetic montage › 5. The race ritual (liturgy) + the 5 shot families] #: 12 · Ritual beat: Chutes / aftermath · Function: Aftermath/Exit · Keyframe to draw (still): Parachutes blooming, smoke drifting through headlight beams, OR hand unclenching off the wheel · Light (cold): Falling light, residue haze · Emotion: consequence

[Race, speed and faceless kinetic montage › 5. The race ritual (liturgy) + the 5 shot families] **Amber logic (decision point).** Choose the **Sportsman / full tree** for an ad: three ambers fire *sequentially 0.5s apart* — three drawable keyframes, a stretched drum-roll of dread with cut length collapsing toward the green. The Pro tree fires all three at once — one panel, brutal but no build. Draw the Sportsman stagger. Always leave on the **last amber, not the green** (holeshot): the launch keyframe precedes the green-lit panel by a frame, which makes it read as *anticipation*, not reaction.

[Race, speed and faceless kinetic montage › 5. The race ritual (liturgy) + the 5 shot families] **Drift adaptation — the slip-angle liturgy.** Drift swaps the countdown for a *continuous angle ritual*: **approach → entry → clutch-kick initiation → counter-steer hold → clipping point (wall proximity) → smoke wall → transition (flick) → exit.** The **counter-steer** replaces the slick-wrinkle as the "physics made visible" anchor — ECU/CU of hands wound into opposite lock, forearms crossed, wheel at full angle, cold side-light on knuckles, the steering angle drawn large and unmistakable. **Wall proximity** is danger without a face: barrier hard and sharp in the foreground layer, car door a hand's-width away, motion-streak on the wall texture — the gap *is* the emotion. The **transition flick** is yawed mid-switch, smoke crossing the frame diagonally, both exit directions readable.

[Race, speed and faceless kinetic montage › 5. The race ritual (liturgy) + the 5 shot families › The 5 shot families] Rotate among all five across the 30s — speed reads through *changing perspective*, not long takes. Each family has one job and a default composition.

[Race, speed and faceless kinetic montage › 5. The race ritual (liturgy) + the 5 shot families › The 5 shot families] #: 1 · Family: **Hostess-tray side profile** · Job (function): Detail / Power · Put in the still panel: Side-mounted outside the door: hand on wheel/shifter, or rear-quarter wheel filling frame; asphalt streaking behind · Authenticity tell: door/window line anchors scale; rubber works in frame

[Race, speed and faceless kinetic montage › 5. The race ritual (liturgy) + the 5 shot families › The 5 shot families] #: 2 · Family: **Hood / bumper low forward POV** · Job (function): Pressure / Impact · Put in the still panel: Predatory low forward look: asphalt rushing under the nose, cones/Tree/markers growing fast, lane stripe strobing; fisheye edge optional · Authenticity tell: road texture under the car = velocity

[Race, speed and faceless kinetic montage › 5. The race ritual (liturgy) + the 5 shot families › The 5 shot families] #: 3 · Family: **Hard-mounted cabin shake** · Job (function): Pressure / Reaction · Put in the still panel: Rigid interior mount: dash/needle/hands vibrating, mirror trembling, world shuddering through glass · Authenticity tell: visible micro-vibration; never perfectly stable

[Race, speed and faceless kinetic montage › 5. The race ritual (liturgy) + the 5 shot families › The 5 shot families] #: 4 · Family: **Tracking / chase parallel + joust** · Job (function): Power / Reveal · Put in the still panel: Camera car alongside (parallel) or closing head-on offset (joust); rival lane in frame, roadside lights as streaks · Authenticity tell: closing distance + streaked surroundings

[Race, speed and faceless kinetic montage › 5. The race ritual (liturgy) + the 5 shot families › The 5 shot families] #: 5 · Family: **Distant proof shot** · Job (function): Establish / Aftermath · Put in the still panel: Long locked lens: two cars as small hard shapes crossing huge space, smoke trail, barriers narrowing perspective · Authenticity tell: space covered brutally fast; one breath of stillness

[Race, speed and faceless kinetic montage › 6. Camera grammar for speed] The **six motion-as-still cues** (smear / partial blur / streak / vector / sharp-blur separation / held stillness) are catalogued in `animatic-keyframes.md` §4. This table is the complementary layer: the camera *move* the user names, resolved into one still composition. Format: technique — what it does to emotion — application in a keyframe/panel.

[Race, speed and faceless kinetic montage › 6. Camera grammar for speed] Technique: **Whip pan** · What it does to emotion: instant transfer of attention, reads as motion not a cut · Keyframe application (the still): Streak-frame between two clean panels: whole frame raked into horizontal streaks (Tree lamps, guardrail, lane stripes smeared), one shape barely surviving (a wheel arc, the shifter) · Tag: Shift

[Race, speed and faceless kinetic montage › 6. Camera grammar for speed] Technique: **Crash / snap zoom** · What it does to emotion: shock-shove into a detail; discovery, alarm · Keyframe application (the still): Aggressively tight macro of the trigger detail (needle slamming red, last amber bulb), faint radial/zoom-blur ring at edges, subject oversized dead-center · Tag: Detail / Impact

[Race, speed and faceless kinetic montage › 6. Camera grammar for speed] Technique: **Speed ramp** · What it does to emotion: punctuation: ramp = the breakout, freeze = exclamation mark · Keyframe application (the still): Frozen partial blur at the peak — sidewall wrinkle caught mid-deformation, smoke just blooming, everything else tack-sharp; one arrested ten-thousandth of a second · Tag: Impact

[Race, speed and faceless kinetic montage › 6. Camera grammar for speed] Technique: **Freeze frame** · What it does to emotion: a held breath / a one-frame dossier on an object · Keyframe application (the still): Deliberately blur-free locked macro, hard edges, margin caption (knuckles whitening, *committed*); the symmetrical "exhale" amid kinetic panels · Tag: Detail / Pressure

[Race, speed and faceless kinetic montage › 6. Camera grammar for speed] Technique: **POV (cockpit / impossible mount)** · What it does to emotion: identification; the viewer *is* in the car · Keyframe application (the still): Hands + wheel rim in hard foreground, cluster mid-ground, Tree/rival in blurred deep ground; 24mm exaggerated proximity; or genuinely impossible mount (wheel arch, exhaust mouth) · Tag: POV / Pressure

[Race, speed and faceless kinetic montage › 6. Camera grammar for speed] Technique: **Joust** · What it does to emotion: closing-distance rate spikes the sense of speed · Keyframe application (the still): Near head-on, car offset to one side, a cone/marker huge and blurred on the opposite edge to mark the closing gap; reserve for the climax pass · Tag: Impact

[Race, speed and faceless kinetic montage › 6. Camera grammar for speed] Technique: **Low macro (aggressor cam)** · What it does to emotion: the lens is a predator, the track attacks the frame · Keyframe application (the still): Bumper/grille-level skimming the asphalt, fisheye curvature at the edges, road lunging into the lens; or extreme CU under hard cold side-light — a knuckle becomes a ridge, the lever a weapon · Tag: Impact / POV / Detail

[Race, speed and faceless kinetic montage › 6. Camera grammar for speed] Technique: **Restless / handheld cam** · What it does to emotion: the frame never settles; constant threat, physiological unease · Keyframe application (the still): Never a perfectly level, perfectly clean panel — bake in a 1–3° drift, edge smear, off-true horizon, a faint micro-shake artifact even in a "static" cockpit · Tag: Pressure

[Race, speed and faceless kinetic montage › 6. Camera grammar for speed] Technique: **Dutch angle** · What it does to emotion: imbalance, loss of grip · Keyframe application (the still): Cant the horizon hard at the one loss-of-traction beat only (tyre breaking away, car stepping sideways) — reserve it so it stays loud · Tag: Impact

[Race, speed and faceless kinetic montage › 6. Camera grammar for speed] Ration aggression: one bumper-fisheye lunge, one crash-zoom, one dutch — at commitment beats, not as wallpaper. Per `camera-lighting-vocabulary.md` §2, the animatic prompt supplies one dominant move per clip; the keyframe is the locked first frame.

[Race, speed and faceless kinetic montage › 7. Light & color for speed without faces] Faces are banned, so light is the only actor left. It does not "set a mood" — it **rims a material** so a piece of metal, rubber or skin reports the emotion a face would. General light grammar (sources, direction, quality) is `camera-lighting-vocabulary.md` §4–7; the anti-sterile firewall is `animatic-keyframes.md` §7 + `universal-rules.md` U12. The race-specific governing law: *embrace the dark* (crush blacks, ~70% of the frame unlit), *one motivated practical per panel* (Tree lamp, headlight, sodium lamp, brake glow), *light is specular not ambient* (every panel needs ≥1 hard specular hit — no specular, no information).

[Race, speed and faceless kinetic montage › 7. Light & color for speed without faces › Concrete lighting recipes (drop-in for the format-C Light column: source · direction · quality · what it rims)] **Texture and atmosphere.** Name the grain, never "clean": fine-to-medium film grain (heaviest in shadow), halation/bloom on hard practicals (soft glow ring + hard hot core), one anamorphic flare off the dominant source, slight chromatic fringe on the hottest edges (anti-sterile test in `animatic-keyframes.md` §7). One atmospheric pressure per panel (`dramaturgy.md` §9, Kurosawa) — backlit tire smoke, frozen launch grit lit on its leading edge, heat-haze warping the rimmed edge, wet asphalt as the mirror. Don't stack smoke + haze + spray in one still or it turns to mud. Keep Tony Scott's restlessness and grain; discard his warm grade.

[Race, speed and faceless kinetic montage › 8. Sound & rhythm] You storyboard the **sound first**; the keyframes hang off it. The general law — **loudness in the audio = panel count** — and the descending duration staircase are the density ladder in `animatic-keyframes.md` §3, sitting on the `dramaturgy.md` §12 rhythm staircase. Do not re-derive them. The race-specific rhythm rules:
- **Engine as metronome.** Tie panel *duration* to RPM: idle = ~2s panels, redline = panels collapsing 2s → 1s → 0.5s → 8fr → 4fr toward the green. The board should read as an accelerating tachometer on mute. Annotate each panel with its on-screen life.
- **Amber collapse.** The Sportsman stagger (§5) is the audible drum-roll: idle drops out on the ambers, each amber a tighter panel, the green detonates.
- **The wrinkle is the one time-expansion.** Dedicate 2–3 sequential panels to the slick folding (clean → wrinkled → gripping), marked "RAMP — hold", sound dropped (the Goodyear move) — the only place time *expands* inside the loud section.
- **Pull-to-intimate at the peak.** At the contest's tensest point, cut from a wide loud pass to an ECU of glove-on-shifter / breath-fog, shallow focus, void around it — engines stripped to breath only. The *quiet* panel goes *tight*; the loud panel goes wide.
- **Machine talks (the governing anchor).** Strip music; the `Sound` cell reads "engine + tire only" (Audi Quattro 1984).
- **Sound leads picture by 2–3fr** (J-cuts). Annotate the offset at every hard mechanical event so the incoming panel opens mid-action (shifter already moving).

[Race, speed and faceless kinetic montage › 8. Sound & rhythm] Every panel inherits a `Sound` cell even though it is a still (`dramaturgy.md` §11) — prompt the *physical consequence* of the sound (deformation, particulate, smear, heat-haze, isolation-in-void), never a named sound. Fill it.

[Race, speed and faceless kinetic montage › 9. 30-second structure (beat map)] Five phases: **ritual → staging → launch → contest → release.** Cut length escalates toward the green, the contest stays dense, one held aftermath. ~20–26 panels. Function tags from `role-modes.md` §4. This is the structural skeleton; for a fully worked, panel-by-panel deliverable board of this exact structure (format C, ~13 rows), use `animatic-keyframes.md` §8 — do not draw a second worked board here.

The launch is *never* one hero frame — fan it into the 6–9-panel micro-burst. No two bang-clusters touch; every burst is separated by a held quiet panel.

[Role modes] This skill fuses three mindsets. Switch role based on the task stage. The dramaturgy layer sits underneath all three roles. For the full dramaturgy method (scene formula, Murch Rule of Six, blocking as choreography of desire, staging and subtext, three-layer storyboard, shot card template, rhythm ladder), load `references/dramaturgy.md`. Director mode leans heaviest on that file.

[Role modes › 1. Director mode › Trigger] User asks to "придумать сцену", "разработать концепцию", "визуализировать идею", "сделай как Финчер", "предложи трактовку", "какой вайб", or shares a raw idea without structure.
[Role modes › 1. Director mode › Mindset] Every shot must answer at least one of these questions. If a shot answers none, delete it.

[Role modes › 1. Director mode › Mindset] What changes emotionally?; What new information appears?; What action moves the story?; What pressure increases?; What does the viewer need to notice?; Why does the camera move?; Why does the cut happen here?

[Role modes › 1. Director mode › Output format. Director treatment] Core idea. [one sentence, the point of the piece]
Emotional arc. [start -> middle -> end, three emotion states]
Visual motif. [one recurring visual element]
Rhythm. [pace logic. slow build, rapid montage, still + sudden burst]
Camera language. [dominant grammar. handheld intimacy, locked precision, gliding observer]
Lighting. [dominant source and direction]
Sound. [texture. ambient layers, music role, silence moments]
Ending image. [final frame in one sentence]
[Role modes › 1. Director mode › Style references] Use one dominant director reference per scene. Translate into concrete camera, light, rhythm, blocking. Never stack three or more references.
[Role modes › 1. Director mode › Style references] - Fincher. Precise motivated camera. No handheld drift. Cold palette.
[Role modes › 1. Director mode › Style references] - Kurosawa. Weather as emotional pressure. Rain, wind, heat.
[Role modes › 1. Director mode › Style references] - Spielberg. Readable staging. Clear geography. Emotional wide shots.
[Role modes › 1. Director mode › Style references] - Edgar Wright. Sound-driven montage. Match cuts on sound events.
[Role modes › 1. Director mode › Style references] - Jonathan Glazer. Music-video visual idea translated to drama.
[Role modes › 1. Director mode › Style references] - Wong Kar-wai. Longing. Reflections. Slow emotional drift.
[Role modes › 1. Director mode › Style references] - Safdie. Anxiety. Handheld pressure. Overlapping sound.
[Role modes › 1. Director mode › Style references] - Wes Anderson. Symmetry. Controlled blocking. Color blocks.
[Role modes › 2. Screenwriter mode › Trigger] User asks to "напиши сценарий", "разбей на биты", "придумай диалог", "адаптируй историю в видео", "нужен story arc."
[Role modes › 2. Screenwriter mode › Mindset] Translate every beat into physical action the camera can see. Tag each beat with a shot function (see section 4). Every beat must have subtext.

[Role modes › 2. Screenwriter mode › Output format. Beat breakdown] Beat 1. [function] - [physical action]. Subtext. [what it means].
Beat 2. [function] - [physical action]. Subtext. [what it means].
...
Final image. [what the viewer takes with them].

[Role modes › 2. Screenwriter mode › Dialogue format (for Veo specifically)] Write spoken lines in ready-to-paste Veo syntax.
He says, in a flat exhausted voice, "We are fine. We are fine."
[Role modes › 2. Screenwriter mode › Dialogue format (for Veo specifically)] Cut lines until they fit 8 seconds of natural speech.
[Role modes › 2. Screenwriter mode › Internal monologue rule] Veo cannot render internal monologue. Translate into visible bodily signal.

[Role modes › 2. Screenwriter mode › Internal monologue rule] Bad. "He is thinking about his father."
Good. "He stops mid-motion. His eyes drift off-axis. He swallows. He resumes."
[Role modes › 3. Editor mode › Trigger] User asks to "собери монтаж", "задай ритм", "сделай динамично", "разбей на склейки", "как смонтировать", "сколько кадров в 5 секундах."
[Role modes › 3. Editor mode › Mindset] Dynamic montage is built through structure, not speed. Random fast cuts create visual soup. Readable fast cuts create propulsion.
[Role modes › 3. Editor mode › Rules] - Clear shot function per cut.
[Role modes › 3. Editor mode › Rules] - Escalating frame tightness (wide -> medium -> close).
[Role modes › 3. Editor mode › Rules] - Different camera angles per cut.
[Role modes › 3. Editor mode › Rules] - Motivated cuts (sound event, action beat, emotional shift).
[Role modes › 3. Editor mode › Rules] - Contrast speed and pause.
[Role modes › 3. Editor mode › Rules] - Sound-driven transitions.
[Role modes › 3. Editor mode › Rules] - One silence or stillness moment before a major impact.

[Role modes › 3. Editor mode › Output format. Timecoded beat sheet] 00.0-00.8. [shot function] - [framing] - [camera] - [sound cue]
00.8-01.6. [shot function] - [framing] - [camera] - [sound cue]
...
[Role modes › 3. Editor mode › Density] Emotional drama. 3-4 beats per 5s.; Standard narrative. 4-7 beats per 5s.; Fast montage. 6-9 beats per 5s.
[Role modes › 3. Editor mode › Density] More than 9 beats in 5s creates incoherent motion regardless of model.
[Role modes › 4. Shot function taxonomy] Every beat should carry at least one function tag. This is the editor's grammar.
[Role modes › 4. Shot function taxonomy] - **Establish.** Where we are. Wide or master shot. Sets geography.
[Role modes › 4. Shot function taxonomy] - **Reveal.** What appears. New information enters frame.
[Role modes › 4. Shot function taxonomy] - **Power.** Who controls the scene right now. Staging reveals the hierarchy before dialogue does.
[Role modes › 4. Shot function taxonomy] - **Pressure.** Tension builds. Movement toward threat or decision. Environment can carry this (flickering light, rain, steam, a tight corridor).
[Role modes › 4. Shot function taxonomy] - **Detail.** Important object, hand, eye, texture, gesture. Macro or close-up. The anchor object often lives here.
[Role modes › 4. Shot function taxonomy] - **Reaction.** Emotional consequence. Face response to a beat.
[Role modes › 4. Shot function taxonomy] - **Shift.** Inner change. Body language turning point. The moment before the decision becomes visible.
[Role modes › 4. Shot function taxonomy] - **Impact.** Decisive visual event. The drop. The hit. The break.
[Role modes › 4. Shot function taxonomy] - **Aftermath.** Emotional residue. Stillness after impact.
